newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares slip, seen drifting sideways.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares slip, seen drifting sideways.

text.p: Slovenian shares eased 0.27 percent on Wednesday and brokers said they expected the market to show little movement for the rest of the week.
"It was a very quiet trading day and were it not for interest in the shares of newly privatised firms Lek and Kolinska, turnover -- which is already low -- would've been even lower," one broker said.
* The seven-share SBI index fell 2.50 points to 931.18.
* Eight shares fell and seven rose, while nine were untraded.
* Turnover rose to 168.2 million tolars from 165.3 million.
* New shares of drug producer Lek were the most actively traded, firming 1.20 percent to 15,813 tolars on volume of 7,947 shares for total turnover of 125.7 million tolars.
* Bank Hipotekarna banka Brezice was the leading decliner, tumbling 8.48 percent to 3,194 tolars on volume of 220 shares for total turnover of 703,000 tolars.
* Lek's old shares were the biggest gainer, firming 3.60 percent to 15,672 tolars on volume of 204 shares for total turnover of 3.2 million tolars.
* Food producer Kolinska rose 0.08 percent to 1,537 tolars on volume of 12,795 shares for total turnover of 19.7 million tolars. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsrom, 386-61-125-8439
